The frame loop hands the CPU an instruction budget. The CPU executes
one instruction at a time through the

core, and every memory
access the instruction makes is routed through the bus adapter and

(CCK, 3.546895 MHz -- the chip bus clock).
The experimental

runs batches instead, bounded by hardware
deadlines: up to 4096 instructions of code in fast RAM or ROM, one
instruction of code in chip RAM. It reads fast RAM and ROM directly, so
only chip-bus and device accesses take the bus adapter (see

). The precise CPU loop selects its diagnostic-capable or
branch-free normal form once per slice. Arming a debugger, trace,
watchpoint, waveform PC trigger or diagnostic recorder selects the
former; normal and browser runs therefore do not retest every inactive
hook after every instruction. An instruction-granular control stop
retains the unfinished budget and its

; resume completes that same quantum
before starting another, so a host-side observation cannot move an
emulated interrupt race by repartitioning the execution loop.

Advancing the clock for a CPU access also advances everything else:
Agnus beam counters, Copper fetches, blitter slots, Paula audio and disk
DMA, CIA timers. (Devices the CPU can only observe through their
registers are ticked in batches, flushed before any access that could
observe them; see

.)

Every texture upload for a frame (the picture the scaler samples, the RTG
board frame and its UI atlas) runs inside that draw callback, after the
surface has been acquired. A wgpu queue write is staged until the next
submit, and a skipped present has none: macOS reports a covered, minimized
or other-Space window as occluded, and pixels returns that as

without submitting. Uploading before the acquire left one staged copy of
the frame behind for every frame the window stayed hidden, so an RTG
session in a covered window grew by its board frame size times the refresh
rate (about 95 MB/s at 800x600 16-bit) until the host ran out of memory.
As a backstop,

On the small-box machines (A1000/A500/A2000/CDTV), Gary’s coarse decode
mirrors the custom-chip registers throughout the chip-register space where
nothing else answers: the ranger space above the fitted slow RAM in

the mirror answers -- on a floating bus KS 1.2 sizes RAM into unmapped
space and dies on a yellow screen. Machines with a Gayle or Fat
Gary/Ramsey decode the space properly and have no mirror.

carries the A500’s Gary, so the profile is only the fitted parts (8372A

does not model yet: CIA-A’s TOD input can be jumpered to the power supply’s
50/60 Hz mains tick instead of VSYNC (every profile clocks it from VSYNC),
Buster’s Zorro II bus arbitration is implicit in the board DMA paths rather
than modelled as a chip, the slot count is not enforced (the autoconfig
chain takes as many boards as fit the address space), and the CPU slot and
the inactive ISA slots carry nothing.

A CPU read of an address no region claims floats to the last value the
chip data bus carried (

), as on real Agnus-arbitrated
hardware -- not a fixed all-ones pattern. DMA fetches drive that bus, and
so do a 68000’s or 68010’s own fetches and writes, because those CPUs share
the 16-bit chip data bus with Agnus (

);
an unmapped read straight after an instruction fetch therefore floats to
the instruction stream. The 68020 and later run on their own local bus and
do not echo their transfers into it. The difference from a constant
matters: software that chases a pointer off into unmapped space (e.g. a
filesystem walking a corrupted buffer-cache chain) can loop forever on a
fixed value, where the ever-changing floating value lets the chase wander
to a zero terminator as on silicon. Device windows that decode their own
floating bus keep their own values -- e.g. the A2091 board’s unpopulated
XT-interface bytes read
from its own model, not the chip data bus.

Write-only and unmapped custom-register offsets float the same way: the
chips decode the address but drive no data, so

returns
the bus residue rather than the register’s internal latch (which the
debugger still inspects separately). Each driven word cycle recharges the
bus, so a longword read pairing a readable register with a write-only one
floats the second word to the first --

reads INTREQR
in both halves. Software that reads a write-only register back and ORs the
result into a fresh write therefore picks up garbage bits exactly as on
real hardware: a floating BPLCON3 LOCT bit, for example, misroutes AGA
palette writes into the low nibbles and darkens the whole palette. The one
deliberate exception is DENISEID (

) cannot false-match a residue; see

With fixed configuration, media, clock seeds, and timestamped inputs,
the core advances deterministically. Audio is generated in emulated time;
window pacing and render-worker scheduling do not change the guest timeline.
This supports repeatable headless captures and snapshot replay.
